title: perf(library): seed starter books from catalog metadata instead of opening the EPUBs
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

On a first visit, add the starter books (runtime config `demoBookUrls`) without downloading parts of each EPUB; fetch the book only when it is opened.

## Why

First visits still read about 1.6 MB of the two starter books (narrated Alice in Wonderland, 10.8 MB, and The Yellow Wallpaper, 15.9 MB) through range requests: 20 fetches of about 129 KB, the same file read several times. Since a recent change, this starts after the page loads (idle), so it no longer delays the first screen, but it still costs data on mobile and competes with cover loading.

## How

- Fork: `src/app/library/hooks/useDemoBooks.ts` imports each URL with `appService.importBook(url, [], { saveBook: false })`, which opens the EPUB remotely (zip directory + metadata + cover). Instead build the library entries from the catalog: the catalog API (`catalog_work`/`fb_card`, `src/services/gutenbergLibrary.ts`) already returns title, author, language, cover URL, size and the file URL/hash for a work. Seed `Book` records from that and import the file on open (as Discover does via `src/services/openCatalogBook.ts`).
- Alternatively, find why the same EPUB is range-read several times (remote zip reader in the fork's document loading) and cache the central directory; that also helps streamed books.

## Working on this fork (read first)

## What

## Why

After a recent change, the library page loads 3,238 KB of JavaScript (decoded). The largest remaining chunks include `foliate`/`MediaOverlay` (about 220 KB) and a chunk with `ollama`, `openai`, `franc`, `supabase` and `MediaOverlay` (about 190 KB). A webpack analysis build listed `ai-sdk-ollama` (301 KB), `@ai-sdk/*`, `zod` (136 KB), `nunjucks` (92 KB), `franc-min` (83 KB), `marked`, `@mozilla/readability` and `react-virtuoso` in the library page's initial chunks.

title: fix(a11y): library page accessibility (contrast, zoom, accessible names, roles)
body:
## Origin

Follow-up from a performance and usability audit of the Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free), November 2026.

## What

Fix the Lighthouse accessibility failures on the library page (score 90): text contrast, disabled zoom, accessible names that don't match visible labels, and invalid ARIA roles.

## Why

Audit P3-13..16. Disabling pinch-zoom is a WCAG 1.4.4 failure; low-contrast secondary text is hard to read in sunlight and for low-vision readers.

## How

- **Contrast (23 elements)**: secondary text uses `text-base-content/60` (authors on cards, 'See all'). Raise to a ratio of at least 4.5:1 for small text (e.g. `/75`) in light and dark themes.
- **Zoom**: the viewport meta has `maximum-scale`/`user-scalable=no` (`src/app/layout.tsx` viewport export). Allow zoom on library pages; if the reader needs to block browser zoom (it has its own), scope that to the reader route.
- **Accessible names (21)**: cards are labelled 'Title, Author' while showing a truncated title; 'Language' shows 'EN'. Make the visible label part of the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3), e.g. `aria-label='Language: English (EN)'` with the visible code inside it.
- **Roles (3)**: `<details role="none" class="dropdown ...">` in dropdowns; remove the role or use a valid element.
- Re-run Lighthouse and `npx @axe-core/cli` (or Playwright + axe) on library, Discover and reader.

## Working on this fork (read first)

This is the **Librebooks** fork of Readest. Its work branch is **`gutenberg-ai`** (the default branch). The Librebooks web app (https://app.librebooks.free) and Android app are built from commits on it.

- Branch from `origin/gutenberg-ai`; open the PR **against `gutenberg-ai` in `superdav42/readest`**. Never open PRs or issues on `readest/readest` (upstream).
- Setup in a fresh worktree:
  ```
  git submodule update --init packages/foliate-js packages/js-mdict packages/qcms packages/simplecc-wasm
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  ```
- Checks (from `apps/readest-app/`): `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`; `npx biome lint <changed files>`; vitest for touched areas: `npx dotenv -e .env -- npx vitest run <test files>`. Record the output in the PR (CI is not relied on).
- Web build for measuring: `BUILD_STATIC_EXPORT=true DISABLE_POSTHOG=true npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next build` (static export in `out/`; serve it with any static server).
- AGPL: every changed upstream file gets `// Modified YYYY-MM-DD for the Gutenberg AI fork of Readest (AGPL-3.0); see MODIFICATIONS.md.` as its first line (new files: `// Added ...`), and the change gets a row in `MODIFICATIONS.md` (newest last).
- Measure before/after (Lighthouse: `npx -y lighthouse@12 <url>/library/ [--preset=desktop] --output=json`) and put both in the PR.

### Hazards

The reader's own pinch-to-zoom and gestures must keep working on mobile.

### Files Scope

- `apps/readest-app/src/app/layout.tsx`
- `apps/readest-app/src/app/library/components/DiscoverHome.tsx`
- `apps/readest-app/src/app/library/components/LibraryHeader.tsx`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Lighthouse accessibility on the library page is 98 or higher with none of these four audits failing.
- [ ] Pinch-zoom works on the library page on mobile; the reader's gestures are unchanged.

```ts
  label: string | null;     // reader name, 'LibriVox volunteers', 'Dramatic reading'; null until readers are looked up
  readers: string[];
  solo: boolean | null;
  dramatic: boolean;
  year: number | null;
  seconds: number;          // length of the whole recording
  sections: number;
  url: string | null;       // the LibriVox page
  own: boolean;             // read from this very ebook (else same title and author, another text)
  status: 'ready' | 'unchecked';   // ready: built, playable with text; unchecked: not built yet
  sample_url: string | null;       // 15 s of the cleaned audio; null until made
}
export interface ListenOptions {
  work_id: number; lang: string; title: string;
  text: { hash: string; url: string } | null;  // the voices text edition (null until a voice is built)
  recordings: ListenRecording[];               // built ones first
  ai: { available: boolean; status: 'ready' | 'preparing' | 'none'; key: string; label: string; sample_url: string | null };
}
```

LibriVox recordings exist in the work's own language only, so `recordings` is empty in other languages; the AI row still shows when `ai.available`. Failure (offline, catalog down) → fall back to what is saved on the device (`savedVoicesListing` in `src/services/tts/voiceOffline.ts`) and always offer **Read now**.

### 2. Route

`apps/readest-app/src/app/book/page.tsx`, `?work=<id>&lang=<code>`; a query-string page, not a dynamic segment (the web build is a static export). Reference for the client-page pattern (`'use client'`, `Suspense`, `useSearchParams`, `useEnv`, `useTheme`): `src/app/player/page.tsx`. Components under `src/app/book/components/`. Safe-area insets: follow `docs/safe-area-insets.md`.

### 3. Rows and buttons

- One row per `recordings[]` (label, falling back to the title when `label` is null; readers, year, length via `formatPlaybackTime`-style helper in `src/utils/time.ts`), then the AI row when `ai.available`.
- **Sample**: new `src/services/listen/samplePlayer.ts`, one shared `HTMLAudioElement`: starting a sample stops the one playing; the button becomes Pause; leaving the page stops it. It streams `sample_url` (served with CORS). A row with `sample_url === null` shows Sample disabled. The AI sample is one clip for every book (the catalog returns the same URL); do not generate anything client-side.
- **Play**: calls `playListenOption(ctx, option)` in new `src/services/listen/playOption.ts`. Minimal version in this issue (#64 replaces the body with the connection-aware version): open the voices text edition (`text.hash`/`text.url`) with `openCatalogBook` (`src/services/openCatalogBook.ts`), `setChosenLibraryVoice(workId, lang, option.key)` (`src/services/tts/libraryVoice.ts:277`), `setPendingTTSAutoplay(book.hash)` (`src/utils/ttsAutoplay.ts`, consumed by `useBooksManager.ts:131`), then `navigateToReader(router, [book.hash])` (`src/utils/nav.ts:115`). When `text` is null (nothing built yet) open the normal best edition as Discover does and set the same autoplay flag; the existing cold-start flows (`VoiceBanner`, `NarrationBanner`) take over when Speak runs.
- **Read now**: the existing open flow, no audio. Extract `openEdition` from `src/app/library/components/DiscoverHome.tsx` (line 535) into a hook `src/app/library/hooks/useOpenEdition.ts` and use it from Discover and the book page, so the "Opening…" progress and error toast behave the same.

### 4. Entry point

`DiscoverHome.tsx` `openCard` (line 682) navigates to `/book?work=<id>&lang=<lang>` instead of opening the reader. "Your requests" rows and My books are unchanged.

## Why

The owner wants the audiobook experience to be the main focus: a reader should see every recording and the AI voice, hear a few seconds of each, and press Play, instead of being dropped into a text edition.

## Acceptance

1. `/book?work=11&lang=en` lists Alice's recordings (built ones first) and the AI narration with Sample, Play and Read now.
2. Sample plays the clip; pressing another Sample stops the first; leaving the page stops it.
3. Play opens the reader at once and starts that voice (the chosen voice is the one pressed).
4. Read now opens the text and plays nothing.
5. Other languages: no LibriVox rows, AI row present when available.
6. Catalog unreachable: saved voices and Read now still show; no crash.
7. Works in light, dark, e-ink (`[data-eink='true']`, use `eink-bordered` / `btn-contrast`), RTL, phone and tablet widths; every new string goes through `_()` (English only for now).

## Verification

- Unit tests (this repo requires the test first): `fetchListenOptions` parsing and fallback; `samplePlayer` (one element, stop-on-start). `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`.
- Real use, Chromium against the live catalog (the acceptance rule in `.agents/rules/acceptance.md`): `npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next dev -p 3210` (if the first start exits at once, start it again); the dev server's `/runtime-config.js` is empty, so serve the deployed reader's `runtime-config.js` through a Playwright `context.route('**/runtime-config.js', …)` (a fresh copy is public at the deployed reader's root). Playwright needs `executablePath` of an installed Chromium on some hosts. Screenshots at most 1568 px on the longest side.
- Say what was not run (Android, iOS) in the PR.

## Out of scope

Download/stream choice, the guard and settings (#64); the Downloads page and delete-when-finished (#65); recordings that do not align (they play as audio only: a later issue).

## Context

Catalog contract: `work_listen_options` (recordings with `status`, `sample_url`; `ai` with `status`, `sample_url`). Voices already published for the AI narration are one MP3 per chapter plus a sync map, the same shape as a LibriVox voice, so Play treats both the same way (`LibraryVoice`, `src/services/tts/libraryVoice.ts`).

title: feat(reader): Play opens the player at once, downloads on Wi-Fi while playing, streams on cellular; size and connection guard
body:
## Pre-flight

- Memory recall: `readest play download wifi cellular` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons.
- Discovery pass: 0 open PRs and no commits in the last 3 h touch the target files.
- File refs verified at the base branch HEAD (b23f10c7): every path and symbol below exists.
- Tier: `tier:standard`. Decisions are made (below). One part needs a device (Android connection type); it ships behind a safe default.
- Base branch: the repository's dispatch base branch. Blocked by #63 (the book page; it defines `playListenOption`). One PR, "Resolves #<this issue>".

## What

**Play opens the player and starts at once. On Wi-Fi the audiobook downloads while it plays; on mobile data it streams.** A size and connection guard protects explicit downloads and has an off switch.

### 1. Connection kind

New `apps/readest-app/src/services/listen/connection.ts`: `connectionKind(): 'unmetered' | 'cellular' | 'unknown'`.
- Web: `navigator.connection.type` (`wifi`/`ethernet` → unmetered, `cellular` → cellular), `saveData === true` → cellular. The API is Chromium only (no Safari or Firefox): then `unknown`.
- Android app: a command in the native bridge plugin (`src-tauri/plugins/tauri-plugin-native-bridge`, `ConnectivityManager`, `NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED`) exposed through `invoke`. iOS: `NWPathMonitor` `isExpensive`. If the native command is not available yet, return `unknown`; do not block the issue on a device.
- **Unknown is treated as cellular** (stream, do not download). Do not change `isMetered()` in `src/utils/network.ts` (it returns false for unknown and Word Lens depends on it); the new function has the opposite default on purpose.

### 2. Play, connection aware

Replace the body of `playListenOption` (`src/services/listen/playOption.ts`, created by the book page issue):
1. Open the voices text edition (small) and the reader, set the chosen voice, set the autoplay flag (`setPendingTTSAutoplay`), as the book page does. The player view opens at once; audio starts as soon as the first track is readable, streaming from the CDN (`LibraryVoice`/`TTSController.#attachNarrationSource`).
2. If `connectionKind() === 'unmetered'`: start `saveVoiceOffline` (`src/services/tts/voiceOffline.ts`) **while playing**. Change it so it can run beside playback: download starting at the track being heard (`controller.currentLibraryTrack()`), then the tracks after it, then wrap to the earlier ones; the sync map first (already). The player already reads each track from the saved copy as soon as it exists (`savedTrackSource` in `resolveTracks`, `TTSController.ts` `#attachNarrationSource`), so no player change is needed beyond not blocking.
3. If `cellular` or `unknown`: stream only; nothing is saved. (A saved copy of the voice is still used when it exists.)
4. A voice that grows (AI narration being made, or a LibriVox voice built track by track): when `controller.refreshLibraryVoice` (`useVoiceOnDemand.ts`) takes a newer build and a download is active for it, top it up with the new tracks.
5. A LibriVox recording not built yet: the existing cold start applies (`requestVoice`, original recording meanwhile, `VoiceBanner`); the download starts when its voice appears. AI narration with status `none`: the existing narration request (`useTTSControl.ts` Speak path, `requestEdition`) applies.
6. Never block playback on the download and never download twice (one active download per voice). Closing the book does not cancel it: it finishes in the background (on the web it lasts while the page is open).

### 3. Guard

New settings (`apps/readest-app/src/types/settings.ts`, `SystemSettings` at line 443, defaults in `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_SETTINGS` in `src/services/constants.ts`; an absent value must read as the default, as the comment at settings.ts:358 explains):

```ts
listening?: {
  guardDownloads?: boolean;   // default true
  guardMegabytes?: number;    // default 100
  deleteWhenFinished?: boolean; // default true (used by the Downloads page issue)
}
```

When `guardDownloads` is on, ask before an **explicit** download (the Listen offline row, `useOfflineNarration.save`, and any button the Downloads page adds) if the connection is `cellular` or `unknown`, or the download is larger than `guardMegabytes`. The dialog states the size (sum of `tracks[].seconds` × 64 kbps ÷ 8, or the real sizes when known) and the connection, with Download and Cancel (use the existing `Dialog` component and the toast/`eventDispatcher` patterns). **Play on Wi-Fi never asks** (it downloads by design), and Play on cellular only streams, so Play never shows the guard. With `guardDownloads` off nothing asks. The toggle itself is placed by the Downloads page issue; here, expose a `useListeningSettings()` hook in `src/hooks/` that reads and writes it through `useSettingsStore` (reference: how `ControlPanel.tsx:166` reads `autoCheckUpdates`).

## Why

The owner wants Play to feel like pressing play on an audiobook: immediate, no choices, with sensible defaults for data use. Streaming on mobile data protects readers from a surprise 100 MB download; downloading on Wi-Fi makes the book work offline afterwards.

## Acceptance

1. Play on a built recording opens the reader and plays within the time the first track takes to start streaming; on Wi-Fi (or ethernet) the tracks appear in storage while it plays, each played from the saved copy once saved; on cellular nothing is saved.
2. Unknown connection: streams, nothing saved.
3. Closing and reopening the book mid-download: no duplicate download, no corrupt track (a partial track is never listed as saved: `voiceOffline` writes the manifest after each finished track).
4. The guard asks on cellular/unknown or above the size, not on Wi-Fi Play; turning it off removes every prompt.
5. A growing voice is topped up.
6. Strings through `_()`; dialog works in dark, e-ink, RTL.

## Verification

- Unit tests first: `connectionKind` for each `navigator.connection` shape; the download order starting at the current track; the guard decision table (connection × size × setting).
- Real use in Chromium against the live catalog with `navigator.connection` overridden (`Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'connection', …)` in a Playwright init script) for wifi, cellular and absent; check Cache Storage keys (`librebooks-voice-offline-v1`) grow only for wifi. Same dev-server recipe as the book page issue.
- Not run unless a device is available: the Android and iOS native commands (say so in the PR).

## Out of scope

The book page layout, the Downloads page UI, delete-when-finished (#63 and #65).

title: feat(reader): Downloads page, delete when finished by default, no progress for partial recordings
body:
## Pre-flight

- Memory recall: `readest downloads storage delete finished` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons.
- Discovery pass: 0 open PRs and no commits in the last 3 h touch the target files.
- File refs verified at the base branch HEAD (b23f10c7): every path and symbol below exists.
- Tier: `tier:standard`. Decisions are made (below). The notes-survive-deletion behaviour must be proven with real notes before the default is switched on (acceptance 4).
- Base branch: the repository's dispatch base branch. Blocked by #64 (it adds the `listening` settings). One PR, "Resolves #<this issue>".

## What

**Full storage control, and a default of deleting an audiobook as soon as it is finished** (the audio and the text edition), while bookmarks, notes, highlights and the reading position are kept and opening or playing the book again is seamless.

### 1. Downloads page

Reachable from the library settings menu (`src/app/library/components/SettingsMenu.tsx`, next to "Manage cache" at line 195; reference window: `CacheManagerWindow.tsx`). A list of what is on the device:
- every saved voice (LibriVox or AI): book title, voice label, size, saved date, a **Keep** toggle and **Delete**;
- total used, **Delete all**;
- the settings: **Delete when finished** (default on), **Ask before large or mobile-data downloads** (default on) and its size in MB (default 100) — the `listening` settings added by the Play issue (`SystemSettings.listening`), via `useListeningSettings()`.

Data: add `listSavedVoices()` to `src/services/tts/voiceOffline.ts` (it already owns the manifest: `readManifest`, `SavedVoice` has `workId`, `lang`, `key`, `savedAt`, `bytes`, `listing` with the voice label; resolve the book title through the library store or the `listing`). Deleting a row calls `removeVoiceOffline(workId, lang, key)` (exists) and removes the text edition with `appService.deleteBook(book, 'local')`.

**Never use `'purge'`**: in `src/services/cloudService.ts` (`deleteBook`) the local action removes only the book file and sets `downloadedAt = null`; `config.json` (progress, notes, bookmarks) and the library record stay, `purge` erases them.

### 2. Delete when finished

New hook `src/app/reader/hooks/useFinishedCleanup.ts`, mounted where `useVoiceOnDemand` is. A book is **finished** when playback of the last narrated section ends (`tts-playback-state` `'stopped'` reached by the end of the book, `emitPlaybackState` in `useTTSControl.ts:152`) or 98% of the voice's audio has played. When it is finished and `deleteWhenFinished` is on and the book is not marked **Keep**: remove the saved voice (`removeVoiceOffline`) and the text edition (`deleteBook(book, 'local')`). Do it when the reader leaves the book (not while the listener is looking at the last page). Keep is stored per work and language in the same `localStorage` area as the voice choice (`src/services/tts/libraryVoice.ts:277` pattern); expose a Keep toggle in the player sheet row (`OfflineNarrationRow.tsx`) and on the Downloads page.

### 3. Seamless reopen

Opening a deleted book again must need no step: a Discover card, the book page or My books re-downloads the text edition and the audio streams (or downloads, per the Play issue). Check `openCatalogBook` (`src/services/openCatalogBook.ts`): `existing && isBookAvailable(existing)` is false for a book whose file was deleted, so it imports again by URL into the same `Books/<hash>/` directory and picks up `config.json`. Make sure the hash is the **same edition** the notes belong to: the catalog keeps every edition at its content hash, so reopen by `book.hash` (not "the newest text edition"); if the work's current text edition has a different hash, offer the reader's own edition first and do not replace it silently.

### 4. No progress for partial recordings

Remove the partial-progress wording: in `src/app/reader/components/tts/OfflineNarrationRow.tsx` the "N of M parts saved…" strings and in `useOfflineNarration.ts` the `saved/total/built` counts used for them. A voice that is still being prepared says "Preparing…", a saved one "Saved on this device"; no percentages for partial recordings anywhere (the Downloads page too). A download in progress may still show that it is working (a spinner or "Saving…"), without numbers for a partial recording.

## Why

The owner wants full control of storage, with a default that keeps the device clean: finished audiobooks are removed automatically, but a reader's notes and place must never be lost, and coming back to a book must just work.

## Acceptance

1. The Downloads page lists saved voices with sizes; Delete and Delete all free the Cache Storage entries (web) or the files under `voice-offline/` (apps) and the manifest.
2. Finishing a book with Keep off and Delete when finished on removes the saved voice and the text edition; with Keep on, or the setting off, nothing is removed.
3. No "N of M" or percentage text for partial recordings remains (search the strings).
4. **Notes survive**: add a highlight with a note and a bookmark, finish the book, confirm the file is gone (`downloadedAt` null), reopen from Discover: the book opens, the note and bookmark are there and the reading position is kept.
5. Delete never calls `purge`.
6. Works in light, dark, e-ink, RTL; strings through `_()`.

## Verification

- Unit tests first: finished detection (end of last section; 98%), Keep and setting gates, `listSavedVoices`, and a test that `deleteBook(book, 'local')` leaves `config.json`.
- Real use in Chromium against the live catalog (dev-server recipe in the book page issue): play a short book to the end with Delete when finished on, check storage and the library entry, reopen it and check the note and bookmark from acceptance 4. Say what was not run (Android, iOS).

## Out of scope

Notes following a reader to a rebuilt text edition (a new hash): the old edition stays available for that reader; mapping old to new sentence ids is a separate decision.

title: fix(reader): Play on a finished book opens at the end and plays nothing
body:
## Pre-flight

- Memory recall: `readest play finished book restart` → no relevant lessons.
- Discovery pass: no open PR touches `playOption.ts`, `ttsAutoplay.ts` or `useBooksManager.ts`.
- Tier: `tier:standard`. Cause is narrowed to one decision point; the fix is local.
- Base branch: the repository's dispatch base branch. One PR, "Resolves #<this issue>".

## What

**Pressing Play on a book that was listened to the end opens the reader on the last page and plays nothing.** Reproduced on the deployed reader (fork commit 6cae4413) with work 1064, en, the AI narration row:

1. Open the book page (`/book?work=1064&lang=en`), press Play, let it play, seek the audio to its end (or listen through).
2. Leave the book (delete-when-finished removes the saved voice and the text edition; notes stay).
3. Open the book page again and press Play. The reader opens at "12 / 14", no mini player appears, and no audio element plays, for at least 30 s.

Expected: Play always starts the chosen voice. A finished book starts again from the beginning; an unfinished one resumes where the listener left off.

## Likely cause

`playListenOption` (`apps/readest-app/src/services/listen/playOption.ts`) sets the chosen voice and `setPendingTTSAutoplay(hash)`; `useBooksManager.ts` (`startTTSWhenReady`, around line 131) then dispatches `tts-speak` at the saved reading position. That position is the end of the book, so there is nothing left to read and the session ends at once (the `tts-session-ended` path in `useFinishedCleanup.ts` treats this as `ended`).

## How

1. In `playOption.ts`, after the book is opened and before navigating, read the book's saved progress (`useBookDataStore` / `appService.loadBookConfig`) and decide whether it is finished: the same `FINISHED_SHARE` rule as `src/services/listen/finished.ts` when a voice share is known, else the saved location is in the last section.
2. If finished, reset the saved location to the first section (the same way the reader's "go to start" action writes `config.location`/`progress`) so autoplay starts at the beginning. Do not touch notes, bookmarks or highlights.
3. If not finished, change nothing.

## Acceptance

1. Steps 1 to 3 above: Play on a finished book plays from the first sentence within a few seconds of the reader opening.
2. An unfinished book resumes at its saved position.
3. Bookmarks, notes and highlights made before finishing are still listed afterwards (sidebar, Bookmark tab).

## Verification

- Unit test first: the finished-or-not decision for a saved progress (last section, 98%, mid-book).
- Real use in Chromium against the live catalog: `npx dotenv -e .env.web -- npx next dev -p 3210` (if the first start exits at a notice, start it again; serve the deployed reader's `runtime-config.js` through a Playwright `context.route`). Seek the playing `Audio` element near its end to finish quickly; the finished book on work 1064 is 13 min. Say what was not run (Android, iOS).

## Out of scope

Which text edition Read now opens (it opens the work's best edition, which can differ from the voices text edition that Play uses; a decision for the owner).

- Memory recall: `readest work groups versions book page` → no relevant lessons.
- Discovery pass: no open PR touches `book/page.tsx`, `ListenRow.tsx` or `DiscoverHome.tsx`; the hot-fix PR that makes Play use each recording's own ebook (`playTarget.ts`) is the base for this work.

The catalog now groups several ebooks of one book (Alice: five). The book page must show that: say which text each recording was read from, offer the other versions, and open the right one. Today `/book?work=28885&lang=en` lists nine recordings with no hint that they come from different texts.

Live contract (public RPC `work_listen_options`, same call `fetchListenOptions` makes; `ListenOptions` in `apps/readest-app/src/services/gutenbergLibrary.ts` already has these optional fields):

```text
work_id            the group's primary (28885 for Alice), requested_work_id the id asked for (11, 928, ... work)
text               the primary's voices text edition, or null
group              null for an ungrouped work, else {primary_id, versions: [{work_id, label, title, default, best: {kind, lang, hash, url} | null}]}
recordings[]       one row per recording, each with work_id (the ebook it is built on), version_label, text {hash, url}
```

The owner decided on 2026-11-24 to group same-text ebooks and show every recording of the group on one book page, with a sensible default text (Rackham-illustrated for Alice) and the other versions selectable.
